prompt: What makes a review from an assistant checkable?
hint: Compare it with "looks good, consider adding tests".

choices.text: That it was written by a model trained on many reviews
choices.why: Training does not make a single claim checkable.

choices.text: That it is short
choices.why: Short and vague is not checkable either.

choices.text: Each finding names a line and a behaviour
choices.why: Right: each one is a claim a test can settle.

choices.text: That it was posted as a comment on the pull request
choices.why: Where it appears changes nothing about whether it can be checked.

prompt: The assistant reviewed `review.diff` alone. What could it not have known?

choices.text: The coupon terms and the tests
choices.why: Right: neither was in the request, nor the shop's time zone.

choices.text: That `today >= until` is in the code
choices.why: That line was in the diff.

choices.text: The names of the coupons
choices.why: They are in the diff.

choices.text: That the code is Python
choices.why: The diff makes that obvious.

prompt: How many findings did the review list?
How does the section check a finding about behaviour?

choices.text: By asking the assistant whether it is sure
choices.why: Its answer is another claim, not a check.

choices.text: By reading the diff again more slowly
choices.why: Reading did not catch finding 1 the first time.

choices.text: By asking a second model for its opinion
choices.why: Two claims are still claims.

choices.text: With a test that fails if it is right
choices.why: Right: the smallest such test.

prompt: Match each finding to how it was settled.

pairs.right: A decision for the owner of the terms

prompt: Why was finding 3 wrong?

choices.text: Python dictionaries ignore case in their keys
choices.why: They do not; the code makes the code upper-case itself.

choices.text: The code is upper-cased before the lookup
choices.why: Right: `code.strip().upper()`.

choices.text: WELCOME10 is stored in lower case
choices.why: The keys are upper case.

choices.text: pytest lower-cases strings in tests
choices.why: pytest changes nothing in the values.

prompt: Why does the section keep the test written for the false finding?
hint: What happens if somebody removes `upper()` later?

choices.text: Because deleting tests is not allowed by `CONVENTIONS.md`
choices.why: The conventions say nothing about that, and lesson 4 section 05 deletes one.

choices.text: To raise the coverage percentage
choices.why: Coverage is not the reason given.

choices.text: It documents a behaviour that works
choices.why: Right: lower-case codes, and it fails if that breaks.

choices.text: So the assistant sees it next time and stops raising the finding
choices.why: Nothing guarantees what the assistant will see.

prompt: How many of the generated tests passed against the code with the off-by-one bug?
Why did the generated test assert that FRIENDS15 is refused on 31 October?
hint: What did it have in its context?

choices.text: It was read off the code
choices.why: Right: the code refuses the 31st, and the test is the bug written down.

choices.text: The coupon terms say the 31st is excluded
choices.why: The terms say inclusive.

choices.text: The model's training data said so
choices.why: Training data knows nothing about this coupon.

choices.text: pytest cannot test the last day of a month
choices.why: It can; lesson 4 section 05 does.

prompt: What does the section say generated tests are good for? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Proving that the code is right
choices.why: A green generated suite says the code does what it does.

choices.text: Characterising behaviour before a refactoring
choices.why: Yes: there, "nothing changes" is the goal.

choices.text: Replacing the specification
choices.why: The specification is where expected values should come from.

choices.text: A starting list of cases to check against the specification
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: For a coupon valid until 31 October inclusive, which pair of dates tests the boundary?

choices.text: 1 October and 31 October
choices.why: Both are valid days; neither tests the end.

choices.text: 30 October and 1 November
choices.why: This misses the last valid day, where the bug was.

choices.text: 2 October and 2 November
choices.why: Neither is at the boundary.

choices.text: 31 October and 1 November
choices.why: Right: the last valid day and the first invalid one.

prompt: After the fix, the generated test fails. What does the section do?

choices.text: Revert the fix, since a test failed
choices.why: The test was asserting the bug.

choices.text: Mark the test as expected to fail
choices.why: It is not a known problem to come back to; it is wrong.

choices.text: Delete the test
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Ask the assistant to regenerate tests from the fixed code
choices.why: That repeats the method that pinned the bug.

prompt: The fix changed `today >= until` to `today ___ until`.
Where should the expected value in a test come from?

choices.text: From running the code and copying what it returns
choices.why: That pins whatever the code does.

choices.text: From the specification: the terms, the ticket, the docstring
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: From the assistant's guess at what the function is for
choices.why: A guess is a claim to check, not a source.

choices.text: From the previous version of the test
choices.why: That only moves the question back a step.

prompt: Both negative rows of the table failed and every other row passed. What does that point to?
hint: One special case, or a class of inputs?

choices.text: A bug in the arithmetic for every negative amount
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A bug in the special case of minus five cents
choices.why: -1290 failed too.

choices.text: A bug in pytest's `parametrize`
choices.why: Six rows passed through the same machinery.

choices.text: Expected values typed wrongly
choices.why: -0.05 and -12.90 are how people read those amounts.

prompt: For `-1290` cents, the original `format_price` returned `___`.
Which edge would a generic list of edge cases most likely miss?
hint: Generic lists know kinds of input, not your rules.

choices.text: An empty string
choices.why: That is on every generic list.

choices.text: Zero
choices.why: Also on every list.

choices.text: A very large number
choices.why: A standard entry.

choices.text: A coupon's last valid day
choices.why: Right: the specification creates that edge.

prompt: The round-trip property passed against the original code, where both functions were wrong. Why?

choices.text: Hypothesis never generates negative numbers
choices.why: The strategy goes down to minus a billion, and the other property got -1.

choices.text: The two bugs cancelled: the wrong text parsed back to the right number
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The seed was fixed, so only positive numbers were tried
choices.why: A fixed seed fixes which inputs, not their sign.

choices.text: Round trips cannot fail for integers
choices.why: One failed after the first fix.

prompt: To what simplest input did hypothesis shrink both failures?

hint: Each fix exposed the next problem.
items: The symmetry property fails at n = -1
`format_price` is fixed to handle the sign

prompt: What does a surviving mutant tell you?

choices.text: The mutation tool has a bug
choices.why: The tool did what it does; the tests did not notice.

choices.text: That line of code is never run
choices.why: Every line here is run by the tests; running is not checking.

choices.text: A behaviour no test checks
choices.why: Right: the one that change affects.

choices.text: The code is correct
choices.why: A survivor says nothing about correctness, only about the tests.

prompt: Why did `//` to `/` survive in `Cart.discount()` before the new tests?
hint: What did every tested discount have in common?

choices.text: Every tested discount divided exactly
choices.why: Right, so both operators gave the same value.

choices.text: Python treats `/` and `//` the same for integers
choices.why: It does not: `598.5` against `598`.

choices.text: The discount is never called in the tests
choices.why: `test_welcome_coupon_takes_ten_percent` calls it.

choices.text: The mutation tool skipped that line
choices.why: It reported it, as SURVIVED.

prompt: 15% of 3,990 cents, rounded down to a whole cent as the shop does: how many cents?
Which role does the section keep away from a review bot in CI?
hint: Which checks are true or false?

choices.text: Reading small pull requests
choices.why: That is one of the things it does well.

choices.text: Pointing a human reviewer at places to look
choices.why: Also something it does well.

choices.text: Posting its findings as comments
choices.why: That is how it informs the person who decides.

choices.text: Deciding whether to merge
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Which settings does the section recommend to keep a review bot's cost sane? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A size limit above which it declines to review
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A higher temperature
choices.why: Temperature has nothing to do with cost.

choices.text: A filter that skips generated files, lock files and vendored code
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Reviewing only on Fridays
choices.why: The bot's value is reading every pull request.

prompt: An assistant generated 40 tests for a payment module and all pass. What should happen before anyone trusts them?
hint: What are their expected values derived from?

choices.text: Nothing: forty passing tests are strong evidence
choices.why: They are evidence that the code does what it does.

choices.text: Check them against the spec, then mutate
choices.why: Right: expected values from the specification, and mutation testing for what they miss.

choices.text: Ask the assistant for forty more
choices.why: More of the same derivation.

choices.text: Raise the coverage threshold in CI
choices.why: Coverage counts lines run, not behaviour checked.
